notes: Rule: A.1 94) 'GOBACK statement (values in the STATUS phrase). Any constraints on the value in the data item or value of the literal in the STATUS phrase are defined by the implementor. This item is required. This item shall be documented' (Annex cites 14.9.18.3 GR10; the rule is §14.9.18.4 GR10 in this text). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-94 |' row in §7 (audit_annex_a1.py lists none; inventory row GAP). The substance IS written in §3's 'STOP RUN / GOBACK termination status' bullet, which labels itself 'Annex A required items 192/193' (192 = the combined STOP-and-GOBACK constraint item, also undocumented as a §7 row) and says 'A main-program GOBACK (§14.9.18.4 GR3) uses the same mapping': integer value -> process exit code, non-numeric operand digit-decoded, host low-8-bit clamp. Behaviour matches the prose (probe at pin: GOBACK WITH ERROR STATUS S(=42) exit 42; NORMAL STATUS "ABEND" exit 0; GOBACK ERROR exit 1; NORMAL STATUS 300 exit 44 = 300 mod 256). PARTIAL only because the determination is not registered under item 94 (the register/inventory mechanism cannot see it); no owning note found (grep DOC-A.1-94 / item 94 in kb/Work: none; PB169 owns the landed behaviour). Edition: Annex E.3 item 32 'The GOBACK statement now allows the same status phrase as the STOP statement' -> 2023 only. cite.py --check 14.9.18.4 'Any constraints on the value of literal-1 or the contents of the data item referenced by identifier-2 are defined by the implementor' -> OK §14.9.18.4 10); cite.py --check A.1 'Any constraints on the value in the data item or value of the literal in the STATUS phrase are defined by the implementor' -> OK §A.1 94).

Rule: A.1 95) 'Hexadecimal alphanumeric literals (mapping for non-existing corresponding character). This item is required. This item shall be documented' -> §8.3.3.2.4 GR5 'The implementor defines the result of specifying a hex-character-sequence-1 for which no corresponding character in that coded character set exists.' CONFORMANCE.md: no '| DOC-A.1-95 |' row (audit_annex_a1.py: absent; inventory GAP), and no §3 prose states it. Code FIXES a behaviour: DecodeHex maps each 2-digit group verbatim to the UTF-16 code unit U+0000-U+00FF, no diagnostic, no exception (probe at pin: X"80FF" -> ORD 129/256, i.e. stored as U+0080/U+00FF; the C1-control range U+0080-U+009F is stored as-is). A fixed-but-undocumented determination = DIVERGES, harm silent. OWNING NOTE: kb/Work/PB1397 (open) already names item 95 in its title ('item 95 (hex-character-sequence with no cor...') — referenced, not re-reported. Editions: GR5 present in 2023; Annex E lists no change to it, so 2014 carries the same rule (earlier editions not derivable from this text). cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.4 'The implementor defines the result of specifying a hex-character-sequence-1 for which no corresponding character in that coded character set exists' -> OK §8.3.3.2.4 5).

Rule: A.1 96) 'Hexadecimal alphanumeric literals (mapping when characters not multiples of four bits). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon a computer's coded character set with characters that are not multiples of four bits. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented' -> §8.3.3.2.4 GR5 second sentence 'The implementor also defines the mapping of each hex-character-sequence-1 to a character, when the characters do not occupy a multiple of four bits.' Code: an alphanumeric character position is one UTF-16 code unit (16 bits, the D-N1 substrate; DecodeHex builds char[] from 2-digit groups; odd digit counts are COBOLNET1635 citing §8.3.3.2.3 r6 — probe X"8" rejected), so the condition does not arise and the item is vacuous. PARTIAL, not CONFORMS: the vacuity rests on a character-width determination (items 12/33 family) that is itself not in §7, and the register counts item 96 among its 195 in-scope obligations (audit_annex_a1.py excludes only 84/85/86/173) while carrying no row that states the vacuity — the project's own convention for a vacuous conditional item is an explicit row (cf. DOC-A.1-185 'VACUOUS - there is no code-name-2'). No owning note found (grep item 96 / DOC-A.1-96: none; nearest is PB1397, which notes 'characters occupy 16 bits ... the second sentence's mapping is not triggered'). cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.4 'when the characters do not occupy a multiple of four bits' -> OK §8.3.3.2.4 5).

Rule: A.1 97) 'Hexadecimal national literals (mapping for non-existing corresponding character). This item is required. This item shall be documented' -> §8.3.3.5.4 GR5 'The implementor defines the result of specifying a hex-character-sequence-1 for which no corresponding character in that coded character set exists.' CONFORMANCE.md: no '| DOC-A.1-97 |' row; no prose elsewhere. Code fixes the behaviour: DecodeHexGroups(...,4) stores each 4-digit group verbatim as a UTF-16 code unit, so a group with no corresponding character (unpaired surrogate U+D800, noncharacter U+FFFF) is kept unchanged with no diagnostic/exception (probe at pin: LENGTH(NX"D800")=1; ORD of NX"D800" = 55297, of NX"FFFF" = 65536). Undocumented fixed determination = DIVERGES (silent). OWNING NOTE: kb/Work/PB160 (open; Registrar 15c paragraph names item 97 and GR-8.3.3.5.4-5) — referenced, not re-reported. cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.4 'The implementor defines the result of specifying a hex-character-sequence-1 for which no corresponding character in that coded character set exists' -> OK §8.3.3.5.4 5).

Rule: A.1 98) 'Hexadecimal national literals (mapping when characters not multiples of four bits). This item is conditionally required ... conditioned upon a computer's coded character set with characters that are not multiples of four bits. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented' -> §8.3.3.5.4 GR5 second sentence. Code: a national character is one UTF-16 code unit (16 bits; DecodeHexGroups perChar=4), so the condition never arises and the item is vacuous in behaviour. PARTIAL for the same reason as DOC-A.1-96: the register counts it in scope (not excluded by audit_annex_a1.py's derived-verdicts) and no row records the vacuity; the national 4-digits-per-character determination (item 122, D-N1) is itself undocumented per PB160's Registrar 15c paragraph. No owning note names item 98; PB160 covers the neighbouring item 97/122 rows. cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.4 'when the characters do not occupy a multiple of four bits' -> OK §8.3.3.5.4 5).
